headline: Visiting Head of State Demands Local Diplomatic Entourage Be Comprised Entirely of People Who Can Whistle 'Dhoom Machale'
body:
Q: With the high-stakes summit approaching, why has the visiting delegation suddenly halted all protocol discussions to conduct nationwide auditions?

A: It’s a very specific tactical requirement. The visiting leader has insisted that every single member of their official Indian reception committee, from the airport ground staff to the senior cabinet ministers, must demonstrate proficiency in whistling the bridge section of the song 'Dhoom Machale'.

Q: Is this a form of code or some kind of high-level diplomatic signal regarding regional trade normalization?

A: Our lead negotiator, Mr. R.K. Sharma, tried to ask that exact question, but he was immediately disqualified for being off-key during his mandatory 'Dhoom' audition. We’ve been told the request is purely for 'ambiance,' and that the normalization process cannot legally commence until the visiting motorcade is escorted by a fleet of silent security officers whistling in perfect unison at 120 beats per minute.

Q: How is the government managing to train high-level officials on such short notice?

A: It’s chaos. We have the entire Ministry of External Affairs currently locked in a basement conference room with a vocal coach from a local Bollywood playback studio. They’ve managed to get the Deputy Secretary up to a passable melody, but the Finance Minister keeps accidentally transitioning into a different track, which the visiting delegation has termed a 'major diplomatic breach.'
